sections.h2: What is Olive Branch, MS, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Olive Branch is a city in northeastern DeSoto County, directly on the Tennessee line, and it is a suburb in the Memphis metropolitan area. It reached 39,711 residents at the 2020 census, which makes it the sixth most populous city in Mississippi.

The city's northern edge is the state line, and Memphis city limits touch part of that border. Southaven lies to the west, while unincorporated DeSoto County surrounds it to the east and south. U.S. 78, Highway 302 (Goodman Road) and Highway 305 (Germantown Road and Cockrum Street) meet here, and the center of Memphis is about 22 miles northwest by U.S. 78.

The city covers about 36.9 square miles. Because it touches Memphis and sits on U.S. 78, the city draws a mix of commuters and people who work in the county's distribution centers.

sections.h2: How did Olive Branch grow so quickly?
sections.html:
Olive Branch was a crossroads village that exploded after 1990. It began as Watson's Crossroad, was established in 1846 and was incorporated in 1873. At the turn of the twentieth century only about 200 people lived there. The first cotton gin arrived in 1910, a public water system in 1922 and electric service in 1927.

The 1990 census counted 3,567 residents. A 1996 annexation to the west doubled the city's land area, and by 2000 the population was 21,054, a 490 percent increase over the 1990 figure. That pace explains why so much of the city is built from newer subdivisions rather than old downtown blocks.

A small historic core remains. Olive Branch Old Towne has a historic trail, shops, festivals and murals funded by a grant. A house near it may be older and on a different lot pattern than the large subdivisions built in the last few decades.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Olive Branch, and why does that matter for sellers?
sections.html:
Warehousing and distribution drive much of the local economy. DeSoto County's economic development council lists Amazon with 3,300 employees, Milwaukee Electric Tool with 3,000, Williams-Sonoma with 1,000 and FedEx Ground with 800 among its larger employers, and Methodist Olive Branch Hospital with 450. Those are countywide figures, and the list includes sites outside Olive Branch itself.

The city's own mayor leans on the industrial base. Mayor Ken Adams started the Olive Branch Mayor's Industrial Council in late 2025, which brings together about 40 of the city's largest employers once a quarter. At its November 4, 2026 meeting, a fact sheet stated that one warehouse produces about the same tax revenue as 415 homes and can create more than 500 jobs. Adams said a single incentivized warehouse would still pay roughly $627,000 a year in school taxes and $283,000 a year in city taxes.

Those taxes help fund schools, the library and infrastructure. For a home seller, the useful point is that nearby land can change use as industrial projects move forward, so check what is planned near your address.

  • Nursing and hospital jobs are hard to fill, according to Methodist's interim CEO at the 2026 council meeting.
  • Hyve Solutions added 300 parking spaces on Stateline Road, and several restaurants and three mixed-use projects were in progress.

sections.h2: What does the Olive Branch housing market look like in the census data?
sections.html:
Olive Branch's 2020 census numbers show very low owner vacancy and high rental vacancy. The 2020 census put the homeowner vacancy rate at 1.0 percent and the rental vacancy rate at 16.1 percent. About 6.1 percent of all housing units were vacant.

With a 16.1 percent rental vacancy rate, a landlord with an empty rental may wait a while for a new tenant. Some owners in that spot weigh a cash sale against renovating and re-leasing.

About 52.5 percent of households were married-couple households, and 36.8 percent had children under 18. The DeSoto County School District serves the city. Buyers who finance with a mortgage will order an appraisal and an inspection, so deferred maintenance can slow a conventional sale.

sections.h2: What permits and code rules apply to an Olive Branch house?
sections.html:
The city's Planning and Development department handles permits, and its Building Department permits all construction and inspects the work. Olive Branch's Code of Ordinances includes a chapter on buildings and building regulations, available on Municode.

The code enforcement page says outdoor sales and storage are not permitted unless city officials approve, and that building permits are required for any accessory building used for storage. If a previous owner added a shed, carport or garage without one, resolve it before you sell. The city's permit forms page lists the code enforcement phone number as 662-892-9342.

The page also says the city enforces ordinances meant to protect public health, safety and quality of life. If you are selling a house you do not live in, ask the city whether any complaint is open against the property.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed and paid in DeSoto County?
sections.html:
DeSoto County bills the property tax, and Mississippi law makes it due by February 1 of the year after the January 1 assessment. The county tax collector has offices in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake, and the phone number is 662-469-8030. Tax receipts can be searched online.

Olive Branch properties pay a county rate and a school district rate, plus a city rate because they lie inside city limits. State law assesses an owner-occupied single-family home at 10 percent of its true value, and the county must revalue real property at least once every four years.

DeSoto County holds its tax sale on the last Monday in August. If a delinquent property is not bought, it passes to the State of Mississippi. Clear any back taxes before closing so the title is clean.

Mississippi's homestead exemption has three tiers. The regular tier gives qualified owners under 65 a tax credit of up to $300. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, are exempt from tax on the first $7,500 of assessed value. Certain disabled veterans and surviving spouses are exempt from all property tax on their homestead. DeSoto County lists a 2027 filing window from January 4 to April 1 at the Tax Assessor's office in Hernando. A buyer's circumstances can change the exemption, so a new owner may need to reapply.

Recording fees at the chancery clerk are set by statute, and DeSoto County provides a fee calculator on its land records page.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Olive Branch?
sections.html:
Olive Branch sellers can list through an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. A well-kept house can do well on the open market. A cash sale is more useful when the house needs work, when you have a tenant, or when you must move soon.

Mississippi requires the seller to deliver a written property condition disclosure statement as soon as practicable before transfer. If it is delivered after an offer, the buyer has three days after delivery in person, or five after mailing, to cancel. Do the form carefully.

We buy houses as-is, with no commission and no closing costs to you. We can review an Olive Branch address, explain how an offer is built, and leave the decision to you.

faqs.q: Is Olive Branch, MS part of Memphis?
faqs.a: No. Olive Branch is a city in DeSoto County, Mississippi, on the Tennessee state line. It is part of the Memphis metropolitan area, and the center of Memphis is about 22 miles away by U.S. 78.

faqs.q: When are DeSoto County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due by February 1 of the year after the January 1 assessment. The county tax collector can be reached at 662-469-8030, and offices are in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake.

faqs.q: When is the DeSoto County tax sale?
faqs.a: DeSoto County holds its tax sale on the last Monday in August. Properties not bought at the sale go to the State of Mississippi.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Olive Branch?
faqs.a: The city's code enforcement page says building permits must be obtained for an accessory building used for storage. Confirm requirements with the Building Department before you build or sell.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption deadline in DeSoto County?
faqs.a: DeSoto County lists a filing window from January 4 to April 1, 2027, at the Tax Assessor's office in Hernando. Statewide, applications are accepted between January 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Must I give a disclosure statement when selling in Mississippi?
faqs.a: In most sales, yes. Mississippi Code section 89-1-503 requires delivery before transfer of title. A late statement gives the buyer three days (in person) or five days (by mail) to cancel.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Olive Branch rental house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often purchase tenant-occupied houses as-is. Review the lease first, and talk to an attorney about your tenant's rights before you sell.
